newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia private sector income seen up 17.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia private sector income seen up 17.7 pct.

text.p: Malaysia's private sector income is expected to grow by 17.7 percent in 1996 after rising 20.3 percent in 1995, the Finance Ministry said on Friday.
In its annual Economic Report, the ministry attributed the moderation in growth to a larger workforce and increased wages against slower growth in corporate revenues.

The manufacturing sector, which contributed more than half of all revenue in the private sector, "is expected to see a sharp deceleration in revenue growth from 23.6 percent in 1995 to 8.1 percent in 1996", the report said.
Export-oriented industries are expected to experience a sharp slowdown in revenue growth to 5.5 percent from 32.3 percent in 1995, the report said.
Among the largest contributors to the slowdown would be the electrical and electronics industry, which is expected to grow by only 3.8 percent in 1996 from 32 percent in 1995.
